program_name: BiRRe - 'Biotechnology for Renewable Resources' curriculum (the English-taught curriculum) of the degree programme 'Biotecnologie Molecolari e Industriali' / 'Molecular and Industrial Biotechnology'. THE DIPLOMA AWARDED IS NAMED AFTER THE PARENT DEGREE, NOT THE CURRICULUM: a graduate of this track receives a Laurea Magistrale in BIOTECNOLOGIE MOLECOLARI E INDUSTRIALI (class LM-8 R - Biotecnologie industriali). 'BiRRe' and 'Biotechnology for Renewable Resources' are internal curriculum labels that do not appear as the degree title; the Italian orientamento profile marks the curriculum simply as 'Biotechnology for Renewable Resources (BiRRe) (LINGUA INGLESE)'. IMPORTANT CORRECTION TO THE RESEARCH OUTLINE: there is NO curriculum called 'Molecular and Industrial Biotechnology'. 'Molecular and Industrial Biotechnology' is the ENGLISH NAME OF THE WHOLE DEGREE, and the degree contains TWO curricula - (1) 'Produzioni Biotecnologiche' / 'Biotechnology productions' (ProBio), taught entirely in Italian, and (2) 'Biotechnology for Renewable Resources' (BiRRe), the partly English-taught one, which is the item researched here. The two curricula have existed since a.a. 2019/2020: 'Il Corso di Laurea Magistrale dall'a.a. 2019/20 e articolato in due curricula'. SECOND IMPORTANT CORRECTION: BiRRe IS NOT A FULLY ENGLISH-TAUGHT TRACK. 30 CFU of compulsory courses inside BiRRe are delivered in ITALIAN, the two elective courses proposed by the Didactic Commission are in Italian, and the internship/orientation module course sheet records its teaching language as Italian. See teaching_language - this is the single most consequential finding for a non-Italian-speaking applicant. OFFICIAL NAME VARIANTS, ALL FROM unina.it SOURCES: Italian legal title 'Biotecnologie Molecolari e Industriali'; English name AS REGISTERED IN THE ORDINAMENTO/RAD is 'Industrial and Molecular Biotechnology' (word order reversed); the orientamento profile, the international course catalogue and the programme website use 'Molecular and Industrial Biotechnology'; the programme website's Coordinator page uses the PLURAL 'Molecular and Industrial Biotechnologies'; the 2025-2026 Didactic Regulations use BOTH forms in the same document ('INDUSTRIAL AND MOLECULAR BIOTECHNOLOGY' on the cover and in Annex 1.2, 'MOLECULAR AND INDUSTRIAL BIOTECHNOLOGY' in Annex 2.1). Internal University course code: D76 (the RAD records 'Biotecnologie Molecolari e Industriali modifica di: Biotecnologie Molecolari e Industriali (1389892)', 1389892 being the MIUR/RAD identifier of the version amended); the CLA placement-test page refers to the master's cohort by the older matriculation code 'matrix N80'. Administering department: Dipartimento di Scienze Chimiche (struttura di riferimento), with the teaching offer also supported by the Dipartimento di Biologia and the Dipartimento di Ingegneria Chimica, dei Materiali e della Produzione Industriale. School: Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base. Teaching area: Scienze MM.FF.NN. Coordinator of the Didactic Coordination Commission: Prof.ssa Daria Maria Monti (Department of Chemical Sciences). DO NOT CONFUSE THIS DEGREE WITH ITS FEEDER BACHELOR: Federico II also runs a three-year Laurea in 'Biotecnologie Molecolari e Industriali' (class L-2, Italian-taught, numero programmato locale, max 150 places) with almost the same name - that seat cap belongs to the bachelor, not to this master's.
teaching_language: MIXED ENGLISH AND ITALIAN - THIS IS NOT A FULLY ENGLISH-TAUGHT TRACK, AND THAT IS THE DECISIVE FACT FOR AN INTERNATIONAL APPLICANT. The parent degree is registered as bilingual: the ordinamento/RAD records 'Lingua in cui si tiene il corso: italiano, inglese', both orientamento profiles print the structured field as 'Lingua ITA/ENG' / 'Language ENG/ITA', and the university's own International course catalogue lists the programme as 'Biotecnologie Molecolari e Industriali / Molecular and Industrial Biotechnology - IT/ENG' (contrast the many Federico II programmes listed there as '- ENG'). WHICH CURRICULUM IS IN WHICH LANGUAGE: ProBio is entirely Italian - 'The lessons of the ProBio curriculum are provided in Italian language'. BiRRe is the English-facing one, but only partly: 'The lessons of the BiRRe curriculum are in English and Italian languages'. THE EXACT SPLIT, RECONSTRUCTED FROM THE OFFICIAL COURSE SHEETS (Annex 2 of the 2025-2026 Didactic Regulations, which state a 'Teaching Language' for every single course, cross-checked against the a.a. 2026/2027 study plan PDF): ENGLISH-TAUGHT COMPULSORY COURSES (6 courses, 57 CFU) - Microalgal exploitation 12 CFU (modules Genetic engineering 6 + Microalgal resources 6), Transport Phenomena for Biotechnological Applications 9 CFU, Biopolymers and Bioplastics 12 CFU (Polyester based bioplastics 6 + Polysaccharide- and protein-based bioplastics 6), Biorefinery processes 6 CFU, Design of conversion processes 12 CFU (Bioreactors 6 + Process simulation 6), Environmental economics 6 CFU. ITALIAN-TAUGHT COMPULSORY COURSES (4 courses, 30 CFU) - Biotecnologie microbiche industriali / Industrial microbial biotechnology 6 CFU, Biotecnologie industriali e per la salvaguardia dell'ambiente / Industrial and environmental biotechnology 12 CFU, Principi di igiene nelle biotecnologie / Hygiene principles in biotechnology 6 CFU, Biochip e biosensori / Biochip and biosensors 6 CFU. Those 87 CFU of taught courses plus 12 CFU of free-choice activities, 18 CFU of internship and 3 CFU of final test give the 120 CFU total. So roughly 66% of the taught credits are in English and 34% - a full quarter of the whole degree - are in ITALIAN, and the Italian ones are MANDATORY, with no English substitute offered. [uncertain] THE PUBLISHED CFU SPLIT IS INCONSISTENT ACROSS OFFICIAL PAGES: the orientamento profiles say 'Lectures for 48 CFU are hold in English language. 30 CFU lectures are hold in Italian language'; the programme website says '6 courses - for a total of 60 CFU spread over a period of one year - are provided in English language and 4 courses - for a total of 30 CFU spread over a period of one year - are provided in Italian language'; the actual course sheets and study plan add up to 57 CFU English + 30 CFU Italian. All three sources agree on the 30 CFU of Italian teaching and on there being 6 English courses and 4 Italian ones; only the English total (48 vs 57 vs 60) differs. FURTHER ITALIAN-LANGUAGE EXPOSURE INSIDE THE TRACK: (a) the free-choice block - the only two electives the Didactic Commission proposes are 'Bio soft matter: fluidi microstrutturati nelle biotecnologie' (6 CFU) and 'Ingegneria dei tessuti' (6 CFU), both Italian-titled; the regulations do allow a student to choose any course in the University consistent with the training project, subject to Didactic Coordination Commission approval, so an English elective is theoretically reachable but not offered by default. (b) The 18 CFU internship module - its Annex 2 course sheet reads 'Course: Internship and Guidance to the World of Work / Teaching Language: Italian'. (c) The final exam - the regulations say the written thesis 'may also be drawn up in English. In this case, an extract in the Italian language shall be attached to it', the orientamento profile says students are 'encouraged to write the thesis in English' and that 'In the case of a thesis written in English, it is mandatory to insert a summary of two pages written in Italian', and the regulations add that 'The presentation is usually in Italian' even though the slides are 'usually in English'. The Italian programme page goes further and describes the final dissertation as simply 'redatto in lingua inglese' (written in English) - a conflict noted below. WHY THE ENGLISH HALF EXISTS: the RAD explains that 'Gli insegnamenti curriculari dedicati alla formazione nel settore delle biotecnologie industriali emergenti saranno tenuti in lingua Inglese' - the courses covering EMERGING industrial biotechnology are the ones taught in English, which is exactly the BiRRe subject matter. A PRACTICAL TRAP: the official ENGLISH-language study plan PDF for a.a. 2026/2027 translates every course title into English and does NOT mark which ones are actually taught in Italian; only the Italian PDF, the Italian orientamento profile (which keeps the Italian titles Italian) and the programme website table (which flags them '(IT)') reveal the split. CURRICULUM CHOICE IS MADE AT ENROLMENT: 'Students must submit a Study Plan (PdS) at the enrolment to select the curriculum.'

degree_class: LM-8 R - Biotecnologie industriali (Industrial Biotechnology). The outline's 'LM-8' is correct but incomplete: the current ordinamento/RAD heads the record 'Classe: LM-8 R - Biotecnologie industriali', the 'R' marking the reformed (riformata) class definition, and the University's index of ordinamenti lists the document as 'LM8 R - Biotecnologie molecolari e industriali'. The unina.it and Dipartimento di Scienze Chimiche course sheets and the orientamento profiles use the bare legacy form 'LM-8' / 'LM-8 Biotecnologie industriali'; both notations denote the same class. STRUCTURE: 2 years, 120 CFU/ECTS, four semesters, conventional in-person delivery ('a. Corso di studio convenzionale'; 'The didactic activity is carried out in presence'). RAD credit envelope: 'CFU totali per il conseguimento del titolo 120', 'Range CFU totali del corso 78 - 169'. TAF breakdown fixed by the 2025-2026 Didactic Regulations: B (characterising) 75 CFU, C (related or complementary) 12, D (student's choice) 12, E (final exam) 3, F (further training activities) 18. Maximum 12 examinations for the degree; integrated courses with two or more modules are examined once. BiRRe study plan for a.a. 2026/2027, in order: YEAR 1 - Biotecnologie microbiche industriali (CHIM/11, 6 CFU, B, Italian); Microalgal exploitation (12 CFU, B, English; modules Genetic engineering BIO/18 6 + Microalgal resources BIO/10 6); Biotecnologie industriali e per la salvaguardia dell'ambiente (12 CFU, Italian; modules Biotecnologie industriali BIO/10 6 TAF B + Biotecnologie per la salvaguardia dell'ambiente AGR/07 6 TAF C); Transport Phenomena for Biotechnological Applications (ING-IND/24, 9 CFU, B, English); Biopolymers and Bioplastics (12 CFU, B, English; Polyester based bioplastics CHIM/11 6 + Polysaccharide- and protein-based bioplastics BIO/10 6); Biorefinery processes (ING-IND/25, 6 CFU, B, English). YEAR 2 - Design of conversion processes (12 CFU, B, English; Bioreactors ING-IND/25 6 + Process simulation ING-IND/26 6); Principi di igiene nelle biotecnologie (MED/42, 6 CFU, C, Italian); Biochip e biosensori (FIS/01, 6 CFU, B, Italian); Environmental economics (SECS-P/02, 6 CFU, B, English); free-choice activities 12 CFU (TAF D); Tirocinio formativo e orientamento al mondo del lavoro 18 CFU (TAF F); Prova finale 3 CFU (TAF E). Free-choice courses proposed by the Didactic Commission for 2026/2027: 'Biosoft matter: fluidi microstrutturati nelle biotecnologie' (ING-IND/24, 6 CFU) and 'Ingegneria dei tessuti' (ING-IND/34, 6 CFU). CFU conventions: 1 CFU = 25 hours of total student commitment; lecture 8 h/CFU, seminar 4 h/CFU, guided exercises and laboratory 12 h/CFU, internship 25 h/CFU. No propaedeutic constraints ('List of propaedeuticities: None'). Attendance: 'In general, attendance of lectures is strongly recommended but not mandatory', except where an individual course sheet imposes it and for credit-bearing seminars, where attendance is compulsory. Marking out of 30, pass mark 18/30, 'cum laude' by unanimous vote. Maximum credits recognisable from prior study: 24 CFU under DM 931 of 4 July 2024; up to 36 CFU may be recognised from single-course enrolments. Job codes attached to the degree in the RAD: Biologi e professioni assimilate (2.3.1.1.1), Biochimici (2.3.1.1.2), Microbiologi (2.3.1.2.2), Biotecnologi (2.3.1.1.4).
admission_type: OPEN ACCESS SUBJECT TO A MANDATORY VERIFICATION OF PREPARATION - not free-for-all, and not a competitive selection either. Both orientamento profiles print the structured field as 'Accesso Verifica di preparazione' / 'Admission Verifica di preparazione'. There is no numero programmato, no ranking, no bando, no admission test and no application fee for this master's. What there IS, and what applicants routinely underestimate, is a formal file review by a named commission, with a discretionary interview attached. THE MECHANISM, from Art. 5 of the 2025-2026 Didactic Regulations: 'Verification of personal preparation is always mandatory, and only students who meet the curricular requirements can access it. The verification of previous knowledge and personal preparation is entrusted by the CCD to the "Access Commission to the Master's Degree" (CALM) - appointed by the CCD - which evaluates the student's career through possible individual interviews. If the CALM considers the level of knowledge and skills of the graduate sufficient, it expresses a judgment of suitability, which allows the matriculation to the Master of Science in Molecular and Industrial Biotechnology. If the Graduate's preparation is assessed as unfit, the CALM identifies the knowledge that the student must acquire BEFORE matriculation.' Note the sequencing: remedial credits, where imposed, must be earned BEFORE enrolling, not during the first year - there is no OFA-style catch-up window at master's level. THE CALM meets 'almeno mensilmente ad eccezione del mese di aprile e agosto' (at least monthly except April and August), is appointed afresh each academic year by the Didactic Coordination Commission, and is fed by a written 'domanda di prevalutazione' (pre-assessment application). AUTOMATIC ADMISSION EXISTS FOR A CLOSED LIST OF FEEDER DEGREES. Table 1 of the access regulation names them: Biotecnologie Biomolecolari e Industriali (curr. Molecolare e Industriale) and Biotecnologie Biomolecolari e Industriali under D.M. 270/04; Biotecnologie per i Prodotti ed i Processi under D.M. 509/99; Biotecnologie (ind. Industriale) under L. 341/90 - all Federico II qualifications. For these, 'La Segreteria Studenti provvede ad immatricolare i Laureati che si trovano nelle condizioni di cui alla tabella 1 senza ulteriori pareri delle CALM' (the Student Office enrols them without any further CALM opinion). The Regulations add that the CCD 'periodically identifies Degree Programmes characterized by educational offer that meets the required entry requirements', whose graduates 'will be able to access the LM without further verification' - so the list can be extended, but the only published version is the 2016 Table 1. EVERY OTHER CANDIDATE, INCLUDING EVERY HOLDER OF A FOREIGN DEGREE, goes through the CALM route. CHANNEL BY PROFILE: holders of an Italian qualification enrol online through Segrepass once the CALM has cleared them; EU candidates and non-EU candidates lawfully resident in Italy or the EU send their academic documents to the course Coordinator for the qualification assessment; non-EU candidates resident abroad must first pre-enrol on Universitaly and obtain a study visa. THE PROGRAMME PUBLISHES NO DEDICATED ADMISSIONS EMAIL for international applicants (unlike, for example, Federico II's Medical Biotechnology, which routes everything through a single address); the operative contacts are the Coordinator Prof.ssa Daria Maria Monti (dariamaria.monti@unina.it), the teaching secretariat Dott.ssa Roberta Ruocco (roberta.ruocco@unina.it), the Student Office contact Dott. Giuseppe Rollino (giuseppe.rollino@unina.it), with ccd.biotecnologieindustriali@unina.it in copy, and the orientation desk infobiotecnologieindustriali@unina.it.
academic_requirements: [uncertain] BECAUSE THE APPLICANT-FACING PAGE AND THE GOVERNING DOCUMENTS PRINT DIFFERENT NUMBERS. Take the lower, current set - see point 3. 1) A FIRST-CYCLE DEGREE (laurea triennale or equivalent). The access regulation phrases it as 'il possesso di una laurea di cui alla tabella allegata al D.M. 270/04 o acquisita nel rispetto dei pre-esistenti ordinamenti, ovvero laurea triennale (ex D.M. 509/99) o laurea quinquennale (L. 341/90)'. Foreign first-cycle degrees are admissible subject to the qualification-recognition route described in required_documents. 2) SUFFICIENT KNOWLEDGE IN FOUR SUBJECT BLOCKS, stated identically in the RAD, the unina.it course sheet, the Didactic Regulations and both orientamento profiles: (a) mathematical, chemical and physical disciplines; (b) biological disciplines (biochemistry, molecular biology, genetics); (c) disciplines of the fermentation sector (microbiology and fermentation chemistry); (d) disciplines of process technologies (thermodynamics and transport phenomena, fundamentals of unit operations for biotechnology). Block (c) and especially block (d) are the ones that most often trip up applicants with a pure life-sciences background: a bachelor's with no transport phenomena / unit operations content is exposed here even if the raw credit counts are met. 3) A CREDIT FLOOR IN NAMED SSD AREAS - AND TWO CONFLICTING VERSIONS ARE IN CIRCULATION. THE CURRENT, AUTHORITATIVE VERSION (ordinamento/RAD approved 22/07/2024 and 25/11/2024; unina.it course sheet; Dipartimento di Scienze Chimiche course sheet; Art. 4 of the Didactic Regulations in force since 2025-2026) is: at least 24 CFU in Area 05 Biological Sciences (BIO/01-BIO/19); at least 6 CFU in Area 01 Mathematics and Computer Science (MAT/01-MAT/09); at least 6 CFU in Area 02 Physical Sciences (FIS/01-FIS/08); at least 16 CFU in Area 03 Chemical Sciences (CHIM/01-CHIM/12). Total 52 CFU. THE STALE VERSION, still printed on BOTH orientamento.unina.it profiles even though they are stamped 'Aggiornata a.a. 2026/2027', is: 30 CFU BIO, 6 CFU MAT, 6 CFU FIS, 18 CFU CHIM - total 60 CFU. A candidate sitting between the two sets (say 26 BIO / 17 CHIM) meets the governing regulation but fails the orientamento page. Apply on the 24/6/6/16 basis and raise the discrepancy in writing with the Coordinator. 4) VERIFICATION IS BY FILE REVIEW AND/OR INTERVIEW: 'Il possesso dei requisiti curriculari e l'adeguatezza della personale preparazione ai fini dell'ammissione vengono accertati mediante esame della carriera universitaria del laureato e/o colloquio, secondo modalita definite nel Regolamento didattico del corso di studio.' 5) ENGLISH B2 IS AN ADMISSION REQUIREMENT IN ITS OWN RIGHT, listed in the RAD immediately after the credit thresholds (see language_requirements). 6) NO MINIMUM GRADE, GPA OR CLASS OF DEGREE IS PUBLISHED anywhere - no 24/30 weighted average, no minimum CGPA for foreign applicants. The gate is credit composition plus the CALM's qualitative judgement. 7) WHERE THE FILE IS SHORT, the CALM 'indica le attivita formative propedeutiche e integrative che il Laureato deve assolvere prima dell'immatricolazione'; the candidate may then requalify either by 'colloquio individuale da concordare con la CALM competente' or by producing 'documentazione amministrativa atta a mostrare il superamento di esami di insegnamenti, eventualmente concordati con la CALM stessa'. 8) NO SEPARATE ACADEMIC PREREQUISITE ATTACHES TO THE BiRRe CURRICULUM. Admission is to the parent degree; the curriculum is chosen by submitting a Study Plan at enrolment. The only differential requirement in practice is linguistic, and it cuts both ways: BiRRe needs working English for 57 CFU and working Italian for 30 CFU. 9) CREDIT RECOGNITION: up to 24 CFU from extra-curricular/professional sources (DM 931/2024), up to 36 CFU from single courses; for transfers within class LM-8, 'the number of credits relating to the same scientific-disciplinary sector directly recognised by the student may not be less than 50% of those previously achieved'.
entry_exam_or_test: [uncertain] NO COMPETITIVE ENTRANCE EXAMINATION, NO TOLC, NO GRE/GMAT, NO PORTFOLIO, NO RANKING. Three assessment mechanisms exist instead, and their operational detail is thinly published. (1) THE CALM FILE REVIEW - always mandatory, a desk assessment of the university career against the curricular thresholds, carried out by the 'Commissione Ammissione Laurea Magistrale' (Access Commission to the Master's Degree) appointed annually by the Didactic Coordination Commission. It normally meets at least monthly except in April and August. (2) AN INDIVIDUAL INTERVIEW (colloquio) - DISCRETIONARY, NOT AUTOMATIC, WHICH IS THE KEY DIFFERENCE FROM SOME OTHER FEDERICO II MASTER'S PROGRAMMES. The RAD wording is 'esame della carriera universitaria del laureato E/O colloquio' (examination of the career AND/OR interview); the access regulation says the CALM 'valuta la carriera dello studente anche attraverso EVENTUALI colloqui individuali' (through POSSIBLE individual interviews); Art. 6 adds that the preparation of candidates outside the automatic-admission table 'sara valutata dalla CALM competente in prima istanza sulla base della documentazione presentata e, SE LO RITERRA NECESSARIO, sulla base di un colloquio individuale' (and, IF IT DEEMS IT NECESSARY, on the basis of an individual interview). So an interview is a possibility triggered by the file, not a fixed step. The Didactic Regulations echo this: the CALM 'evaluates the student's career through possible individual interviews'. NOTHING IS PUBLISHED about the interview's format, language, duration, scheduling or assessment criteria, and no calendar of CALM sittings for a.a. 2026/2027 appears on the programme, department, School or university pages. The pre-assessment form requires the candidate to authorise being summoned informally: 'l'autorizzazione ad essere convocati dalla Commissione Ammissione Laurea Magistrale ... per le vie brevi (posta elettronica o via telefono)' - i.e. by email or telephone, at short notice. An international applicant should assume they may be called and should give a reachable phone number and a monitored email address. (3) THE CLA ENGLISH PLACEMENT TEST - the fallback route for candidates without a B2 certificate, administered by the Centro Linguistico di Ateneo, and note that it is scheduled for enrolled students rather than functioning as a pre-admission screen: 'Students who have non-certified English language skills comparable to level B2 can sit the Placement Test, typically scheduled at the beginning of each year (from January).' It targets 'students enrolled in the LM in Molecular and Industrial Biotechnology (matrix N80) to ascertain the linguistic skills required to be admitted to the CdS (comparable to level B2)'. It 'consists of a series of exercises of various kinds differentiated by level', is sat in university computer rooms - 'Typically the Placement Test takes place in the computer rooms of the Department of Biology' - with venues published on the CLA website and booking made on the ESOL platform. The binding consequence is a mid-course block, not an entry block: 'The English language knowledge requirements must be acquired BEFORE SITTING THE EXAMS OF THE COURSES SCHEDULED FOR THE SECOND YEAR.' (4) NO ITALIAN LANGUAGE TEST is set by the programme itself; if the university treats this IT/ENG degree as Italian-taught for visa purposes, an Italian proficiency test administered under the Universitaly procedure could apply to non-EU applicants - see language_requirements and uncertainty_notes. [uncertain] No 2026/2027 CLA placement-test calendar specific to this programme was found on the pages consulted.

language_requirements: ENGLISH B2 (CEFR) IS THE ONLY LANGUAGE REQUIREMENT THE PROGRAMME ITSELF IMPOSES - BUT SEE THE ITALIAN QUESTION BELOW, WHICH IS THE REAL RISK FOR A NON-EU APPLICANT. ENGLISH: the requirement is stated identically in the RAD, the unina.it and department course sheets, Art. 4 of the Didactic Regulations and both orientamento profiles: 'Inglese - documentata competenza di utilizzare correttamente la lingua Inglese (in forma scritta e orale) equiparabile al livello B2' / 'English - documented competence to use English correctly (in written and oral form) comparable to level B2.' TWO ROUTES TO SATISFY IT, per the programme's own English language skills page: (a) hold a B2 certificate or higher recognised by the CLA - 'Students who hold B2 certificates (or higher) - recognized by the CLA - are exempt from tuition. Students must send the certificate to Dr. Loredana Cavaliere of the CLA for career recognition' ('exempt from tuition' here means exempt from taking the CLA's English teaching, not from paying fees); or (b) pass the CLA Placement Test, 'typically scheduled at the beginning of each year (from January)'. The University also runs CLA courses 'aimed at acquiring skills in the correct use of the English language (in written and oral form) comparable to level B2'. THE DEADLINE IS A MID-COURSE ONE, NOT AN ENTRY ONE: 'The English language knowledge requirements must be acquired before sitting the exams of the courses scheduled for the second year.' In other words a student can matriculate without the certificate but is blocked from all second-year examinations until the requirement is met - a harder practical constraint than it first appears, because in BiRRe the second year carries Design of conversion processes, Environmental economics, the internship and the thesis. NO NAMED CERTIFICATES, SCORE THRESHOLDS OR VALIDITY PERIODS ARE PUBLISHED by the programme (no IELTS/TOEFL band table), and recognition is delegated to the CLA case by case. ITALIAN - [uncertain] AND MATERIALLY UNRESOLVED. The programme sets no Italian requirement of any kind. But the University's rule for non-EU applicants turns on how the DEGREE is classified, and this degree is classified IT/ENG, not ENG. international.unina.it says: '1. If you choose a three-year degree course, magistral degree course or single-cycle magistral degree course in ITALIAN, a B2 level Italian language proficiency is required', to be proved by a CLIQ-system certificate uploaded to Universitaly or by an Italian proficiency test whose 'Procedures and timing will be communicated by e-mail by the coordinator of the chosen course'; and '2. If you choose a three-year, five-year or single-cycle degree course in ENGLISH, level B2 Italian language proficiency is not required.' Clause 2 does not mention two-year magistral courses at all (the same drafting gap affects every English-taught LM at Federico II), and clause 1 explicitly does mention them. On top of that, the University's own International course catalogue lists this programme as 'IT/ENG', and 30 CFU of the BiRRe curriculum plus the internship module really are delivered in Italian. A literal reading therefore points towards ITALIAN B2 BEING REQUIRED for a non-EU applicant to this course, and a purposive reading (the track is advertised in English) points the other way. NO unina.it PAGE RESOLVES IT. This must be settled in writing with the Coordinator and the International Welcome Desk BEFORE the 15 June 2026 Universitaly deadline, because the Italian certificate has to be uploaded with the pre-enrolment application, not afterwards. Practical note: international.unina.it separately advises that an English certificate (IELTS, TOEFL, Cambridge) is 'useful for the issue of the visa by the diplomatic/consular Representation', so hold one regardless. Practical note 2, independent of the formal rule: BiRRe cannot be completed without functional Italian, since four compulsory courses (30 CFU), both proposed electives and the internship module are Italian-taught and the final presentation 'is usually in Italian'.

The initial enrolment is possible until March 31.' That end date (31 March) is nearly five months later than the university notice. Three sources, three windows: 16 July - 2 November, July - 31 March, and 1 September - 31 October. The two orientamento statements also contradict each other. (4) THE STEP THAT ACTUALLY BINDS AN INTERNATIONAL EU CANDIDATE HAS NO PUBLISHED DEADLINE AT ALL. Before enrolling, a holder of a foreign degree must obtain the CALM's judgment of suitability. international.unina.it tells EU candidates to 'send your academic documents to the Coordinator of the course you wish to enrol in to find out whether you meet the enrolment requirements'; for this programme that is Prof.ssa Daria Maria Monti (dariamaria.monti@unina.it), with the teaching secretariat and ccd.biotecnologieindustriali@unina.it in copy. Neither the University nor the programme publishes a cut-off for this step or a calendar of CALM sittings. Since the CALM meets at least monthly except in April and August, and since remedial credits (if imposed) must be acquired BEFORE matriculation, the dossier should be opened by spring at the latest. (5) A SEPARATE, HARD, PROGRAMME-LEVEL DEADLINE THAT APPLICANTS MISS: the Study Plan choosing the free-choice courses is due by 15 OCTOBER, with a correction window for the second semester between 15 FEBRUARY and 15 MARCH ('Il Piano di Studio per la scelta degli insegnamenti a scelta autonoma e presentato entro il 15 ottobre (possibilita di rettifica per il II semestre con presentazione nella finestra 15 febbraio - 15 marzo)'). The Study Plan choosing the CURRICULUM (i.e. choosing BiRRe rather than ProBio) is submitted at enrolment. (6) SECOND-SEMESTER ENTRY is not provided for in any source; treat as unavailable.

A) FOR THE PRE-ASSESSMENT (domanda di prevalutazione) - the decisive course-level submission, set out in Art. 2 of the access regulation. Candidates must attach to the pre-assessment form, which is 'disponibile sul sito della Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base' and delivered to the Area Didattica di Scienze in the Centri Comuni area of the Monte Sant'Angelo complex: (i) 'i dettagli della formazione pregressa, ossia la laurea conseguita, l'elenco in dettaglio degli esami sostenuti CORREDATI DAI RELATIVI PROGRAMMI DEI CORSI e l'elenco di eventuali altre attivita formative, sviluppate per il conseguimento della laurea, ove presenti' - the degree obtained, a detailed list of examinations passed ACCOMPANIED BY THE COURSE SYLLABI, and a list of any other training activities. The syllabus requirement is the heavy one and is easy to overlook: a transcript alone is not enough, because the CALM must judge subject relevance against four named disciplinary blocks; (ii) telephone and email contact details; (iii) written authorisation to be summoned by the CALM informally, by email or telephone. 'Le domande di prevalutazione e la documentazione allegata saranno inoltrate al Presidente della Commissione Ammissione Laurea Magistrale.' The School's form is published as 'Valutazione iscrizione Laurea Magistrale' (https://www.scuolapsb.unina.it/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/Valutazionepre1.pdf), with a companion 'Valutazione carriera pregressa' form; both are image-only PDFs from which no text could be extracted, so the exact fields could not be read. Add the English B2 certificate, since B2 is an access requirement. B) FOR EU CANDIDATES (and non-EU candidates resident in Italy/EU) - the qualification-recognition dossier per international.unina.it: eventual TRANSLATIONS; LEGALISATIONS; DIPLOMA SUPPLEMENT; CERTIFICATES OF EXAMINATIONS; certificates from the Italian ENIC-NARIC centre CIMEA (https://www.cimea.it/EN/); and any DECLARATIONS OF VALUE (Dichiarazione di Valore) issued by the competent diplomatic representations. C) FOR NON-EU CANDIDATES RESIDING ABROAD - documents to take to the Italian Embassy: the SUMMARY OF THE PRE-ENROLMENT APPLICATION submitted through Universitaly and validated by the University; any LANGUAGE COMPETENCE CERTIFICATES; the documents required for the VISA APPLICATION including a HEALTH INSURANCE POLICY where applicable; and the required documents for the foreign qualification. To obtain FROM the Embassy: the type 'D' study entry visa, the stamped health insurance policy and the endorsed qualification documents. D) FOR FINAL ENROLMENT - international.unina.it's 'Documents required for enrolment': copy of PASSPORT; APPLICATION FORM; 1 PASSPORT PHOTO; TAX CODE (codice fiscale); RESIDENCE PERMIT (proof of having applied for it); and the DECLARATION OF VALUE issued by the Italian Embassy in the country where the degree was obtained, or a certificate of validity issued by ENIC-NARIC centres. The page adds the standing caveat: 'Important: always check the instructions on the degree programme's website.' E) VISA-RELATED FINANCIAL AND PRACTICAL EVIDENCE (non-EU): means of subsistence of EUR 10,179.85 per year proven by personal or family financial guarantees or by accredited Italian institutions; the sum needed for repatriation (a return ticket suffices); suitable accommodation in Italy; and adequate medical/hospitalisation insurance valid in Italy without limitations on emergency hospitalisation rates. The residence permit must be applied for within 8 days of arrival at a Post Office, with the application kit, payment slip, a EUR 16.00 duty stamp and the passport. F) FOR HOLDERS OF THE LISTED FEDERICO II FEEDER BACHELOR'S DEGREES: no dossier and no CALM opinion - the Student Office enrols them directly. G) NOT REQUIRED, as far as any published source shows: no CV, no motivation letter, no reference letters, no research proposal, no application fee. [uncertain] Whether the CALM requests further material case by case is not stated, and no English-language version of the pre-assessment procedure exists on the programme, department or School websites.

uncertainty_notes: 1) THE OUTLINE'S PREMISE NEEDS CORRECTING ON TWO POINTS. First, there is no curriculum named 'Molecular and Industrial Biotechnology': that is the English name of the whole LM-8 degree, and the English-facing curriculum inside it is 'BiRRe - Biotechnology for Renewable Resources' (the other being 'ProBio - Produzioni Biotecnologiche', wholly Italian). Second, and far more important for an applicant, BiRRe is NOT fully English-taught. Four compulsory courses totalling 30 CFU are delivered in Italian, both proposed free-choice courses are Italian, the 18 CFU internship module's course sheet records Italian, and the graduation presentation 'is usually in Italian'. Roughly a quarter of the 120-CFU degree is compulsorily in Italian, with no English alternative published. Any listing that presents this as an English-taught master's is misleading. 2) THE PUBLISHED ENGLISH/ITALIAN CFU SPLIT IS INCONSISTENT ACROSS THREE OFFICIAL SOURCES: orientamento says 48 CFU English + 30 Italian; the programme website says 60 English + 30 Italian; the per-course sheets in the 2025-2026 Didactic Regulations and the a.a. 2026/2027 study plan add up to 57 English + 30 Italian. All agree on 6 English courses and 4 Italian ones and on the 30 CFU of Italian teaching. Treat 57/30 as the arithmetic reality and the other two as rounding or legacy figures. 3) THE CURRICULAR CREDIT THRESHOLDS CONFLICT, AND THE APPLICANT-FACING PAGE IS THE STALE ONE. The ordinamento/RAD (approved 2024), the unina.it and Dipartimento di Scienze Chimiche course sheets and Art. 4 of the Didactic Regulations in force since 2025-2026 all require 24 BIO / 6 MAT / 6 FIS / 16 CHIM (52 CFU). Both orientamento profiles, though stamped 'updated 2026/2027', still print 30 BIO / 6 MAT / 6 FIS / 18 CHIM (60 CFU). Candidates between the two sets should apply on the lower figures and flag the discrepancy in writing. 4) THE ENROLMENT WINDOW IS PUBLISHED THREE DIFFERENT WAYS - 16 July to 2 November 2026 (university notice), 'from July ... possible until March 31' (English orientamento) and 1 September to 31 October (Italian orientamento). The two orientamento profiles also contradict each other. Follow the university notice and confirm with segrmmff@unina.it. 5) THE ITALIAN-LANGUAGE REQUIREMENT FOR NON-EU APPLICANTS IS GENUINELY UNRESOLVED AND IS THE LARGEST SINGLE RISK IN THIS FILE. international.unina.it requires Italian B2 for a 'magistral degree course in ITALIAN' and exempts 'a three-year, five-year or single-cycle degree course in ENGLISH' - a clause that omits two-year magistral courses altogether. This degree is officially classified IT/ENG in the University's own international catalogue and really does deliver 30 CFU in Italian. Neither the exemption nor the requirement can be applied to it with confidence, and the certificate (if required) must be uploaded to Universitaly at pre-enrolment, i.e. by 15 June 2026, so the question cannot be deferred. Settle it in writing with the Coordinator and the International Welcome Desk months in advance. 6) NON-EU APPLICANTS FACE AN EARLY, UNFORGIVING CUT-OFF. Because the course is open access, the 15 June 2026 Universitaly pre-enrolment deadline is effectively absolute: the post-15-June concession is reserved to 'programmes with restricted access'. Anyone reading only the 2 November enrolment date would badly misjudge the timeline. 7) THE ADMISSION INTERVIEW IS DISCRETIONARY, NOT AUTOMATIC - a genuine difference from some sibling Federico II master's programmes. The RAD says 'e/o colloquio', the access regulation says 'eventuali colloqui individuali' and 'se lo riterra necessario'. No format, language, timing, calendar or criteria are published anywhere, and there is no published calendar of CALM sittings for 2026/2027; the only stated cadence is 'at least monthly except April and August'. 8) THE GOVERNING ACCESS REGULATION IS NINE YEARS OLD. 'Regolamento per l'accesso al corso di Laurea Magistrale' is footer-dated 'Settembre 2016' and is still the version linked from both orientamento profiles and the programme site. Its Table 1 of automatically-admitted feeder degrees, its reference to a paper application delivered in person to the Area Didattica di Scienze, and its silence on international applicants all reflect that vintage. The document also contains a typographical error in its own subject line ('BIOTECNOLOGIE MOLECOLARI E IDNUSTRIALI'). 9) NO INTERNATIONAL-FACING ADMISSIONS CHANNEL EXISTS AT COURSE LEVEL. Unlike, for example, Federico II's Medical Biotechnology, this programme publishes no dedicated admissions email, no English-language admission page, no application form in English and no instructions for foreign-qualification holders. The procedure has to be assembled from the university-level international pages plus the 2016 access regulation, and first contact is the Coordinator's personal email. 10) FOUR DIFFERENT ENGLISH NAMES FOR THE SAME DEGREE APPEAR ON unina.it: 'Industrial and Molecular Biotechnology' (ordinamento/RAD, and the cover and Annex 1.2 of the Didactic Regulations), 'Molecular and Industrial Biotechnology' (orientamento, international catalogue, programme site, Annex 2.1 of the same Regulations), 'Molecular and Industrial Biotechnologies' (programme site Coordinator page), and in Italian the invariant 'Biotecnologie Molecolari e Industriali'. A diploma-supplement translation could carry any of the English forms; the Italian title is the one that will appear on the diploma. 11) THE COORDINATOR IS RECORDED DIFFERENTLY ON DIFFERENT unina.it PAGES. The unina.it and Dipartimento di Scienze Chimiche SUA course sheets both name 'Prof. Antonio MARZOCCHELLA'; the orientamento profiles and the programme website's own Coordinator page both name Prof.ssa Daria Maria Monti, the latter in terms that describe the current post-holder. Treat Prof.ssa Monti as current and the SUA sheets as un-updated - this matters because international.unina.it routes EU applicants to 'the Coordinator of the course'. 12) A SEAT CAP EXISTS FOR THE BACHELOR OF THE SAME NAME AND IS EASILY MISATTRIBUTED. The three-year L-2 'Biotecnologie Molecolari e Industriali' is numero programmato locale with max 150 places, selected on the school-leaving grade; this master's has no cap. Search engines and aggregators conflate the two. 13) NO SEAT, QUOTA OR SUSTAINABLE-ENROLMENT FIGURE COULD BE CONFIRMED FROM STRUCTURED SOURCES, and no per-course non-EU contingente is published. Both conclusions are inferences from silence. 14) THE THESIS LANGUAGE RULE IS STATED THREE WAYS. The Didactic Regulations and the RAD say the dissertation 'may also be drawn up in English', with an Italian extract attached; the orientamento profile says students are 'encouraged' to write in English and that a two-page Italian summary is then mandatory; the Italian programme page describes the final dissertation flatly as 'redatto in lingua inglese'. There is no rule making an English thesis compulsory for BiRRe students (contrast Federico II's Medical Biotechnology, where the English curriculum's thesis must be in English). Assume English is permitted and encouraged but that an Italian extract is required. 15) TWO CONFLICTING FREE-CHOICE CREDIT FIGURES APPEAR ON THE ENGLISH ORIENTAMENTO PAGE: the study plan says 'Free selection proposed by the student - 12 CFU' while the 'Customizing the study plan' box says 'Students have to submit a PdS to select the free selection of courses (18 CFU)'. The Didactic Regulations and both study plans fix TAF D at 12 CFU and TAF F (internship) at 18 CFU, so the '18 CFU' in that box is a transcription error. 16) THE ENGLISH-LANGUAGE STUDY PLAN PDF HIDES THE LANGUAGE SPLIT. The official a.a. 2026/2027 English study plan translates every course title into English and gives no language column, so a reader using only English-language material cannot tell that four of the courses are taught in Italian. Only the Italian PDF, the Italian orientamento profile and the programme website table (which flags them '(IT)') disclose it, and only Annex 2 of the Didactic Regulations states it course by course. 17) THE PROGRAMME WEBSITE IS HTTP-ONLY. www.biotecnologieindustriali.unina.it refuses connections on port 443; any https:// form of its URLs will fail, and tools that force HTTPS cannot reach the Didactic Regulations, the access regulation or the language page. 18) MINOR DEFECTS IN OFFICIAL SOURCES, reproduced here so they are recognisable when searching: 'Iyalian' for 'Italian' and 'Eropean' for 'European' on international.unina.it; 'IDNUSTRIALI' in the access regulation; 'Accesso al Corso: Laurea di 2 livello' on the unina.it course sheet where a first-level degree is meant; 'Bioecomics and intellectual property' for 'Bioeconomics' on the English orientamento page; the address spelled both 'Via Cinthia' and 'Via Cintia'; and the Italian orientamento slug lacking the '-lm' suffix that the English one carries. 19) THE PRE-ASSESSMENT FORMS COULD NOT BE READ. Both 'Valutazionepre1.pdf' and 'ValCarrieraPregressa1.pdf' on scuolapsb.unina.it are image-only PDFs with no extractable text layer, so their exact fields and any printed deadlines could not be verified; the document list above comes from Art. 2 of the access regulation instead. 20) FEE FIGURES CARRY NO ACADEMIC YEAR. The EUR 200 / EUR 140 / EUR 16 amounts come solely from international.unina.it, which does not say which year they apply to, and for Italian-resident students the contribution is ISEE-based rather than flat, so the figure is a reference rather than a universal charge.
